front.title: An Authorization Disposition Object for Agent Decision Receipts

abstract.t:
A verification check that has completed and a human authorization that is still outstanding can coexist for the same proposed action. Receipt formats that carry only a claim-state enumeration cannot express the second condition, because it is not a statement about the claim: it is a statement about what must happen before the action.
This document specifies an authorization disposition, a sibling object carried alongside check results, and the processing rules by which a consumer derives a fail-closed decision about whether an action may be initiated. The disposition carries a named holder, two distinct deadlines, an action-instance binding, and a detached signed decision.
The document treats receipt integrity, the decision recorded at issuance, and present actionability as separate questions. It distinguishes insufficient evidence from conflicting evidence, prohibits treating an unevaluated authorization requirement as "not required", and specifies requirements for historical verification, replay prevention, and tenant-scoped instance ownership. It records what the object establishes and, equally, what it does not.
